policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'of their substance' renders either ἐκ or ἀπὸ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων identically; the mapped note 'Many ancient authorities read him' concerns the pronoun αὐταῖς/αὐτῷ ('ministered unto them'), not this preposition.
ASV 'other fell on the rock' is the plain rendering of either the compound κατέπεσεν or simple ἔπεσεν; no English element answers to the κατα- prefix.
ASV reports the question indirectly, 'asked him what this parable might be', with no 'saying'; the added λέγοντες would surface in ASV as 'saying' introducing direct speech.
Pure word order within the indirect question; 'what this parable might be' is identical for αὕτη εἴη ἡ παραβολή and εἴη ἡ παραβολὴ αὕτη.
ASV 'are they that have heard' is a completed act answering the aorist ἀκούσαντες; the present ἀκούοντες would give 'that hear', as ASV writes in v. 21 for the present participle.
ASV 'putteth it on a stand' renders τίθησιν and ἐπιτίθησιν alike; the preposition ἐπι- is already carried by English 'on'.
ASV 'that shall not be known' fits both the emphatic subjunctive οὐ μὴ γνωσθῇ and the future γνωσθήσεται; English has no distinct form for the emphatic negation.
ASV 'for whosoever hath' renders ὃς ἂν γὰρ ἔχῃ and ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν ἔχῃ identically; the only note here is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, seemeth to have') and concerns English wording.
ἂν and ἐὰν are equivalent in the indefinite relative; ASV 'whosoever hath not' distinguishes neither.
ASV 'there came to him his mother and brethren' leaves the verb's number unmarked in English, so neither the singular Παρεγένετο nor the plural Παρεγένοντο is excluded.
ASV opens 'And it was told him'; ASV renders both δέ and καί as 'And', so the connective does not settle ἀπηγγέλη δὲ against Καὶ ἀπηγγέλη.
ASV passes straight from 'And it was told him' to the message with no 'saying'; the added λέγοντων would appear as 'saying' before 'Thy mother'.
Word order only; 'desiring to see thee' is the same English for σε θέλοντές and θέλοντές σε.
ASV 'and do it' supplies an object English requires after 'do' whether or not αὐτόν stands in the Greek, so the pronoun does not decide.
ASV opens 'Now it came to pass', and 'Now' is ASV's rendering of an adversative δέ; Καὶ ἐγένετο would give 'And it came to pass'.
ASV 'And he awoke' renders διεγερθεὶς and ἐγερθεὶς alike; no English word answers to the δια- prefix.
ASV 'Where is your faith?' requires the copula in English whether or not ἐστιν stands in the Greek.
ASV text reads 'the country of the Gerasenes' (Γερασηνῶν), and the mapped textual note relegates Gergesenes and Gadarenes to 'many ancient authorities'.
ASV 'there met him a certain man' needs the object pronoun in English regardless; ὑπήντησεν alone would still be rendered 'met him' from the context.
ASV 'who had demons' is an ordinary English relative clause for an attributive participle ἔχων as well as for the finite ὃς εἶχεν.

ASV joins the time phrase to the clothing clause — 'and for a long time he had worn no clothes' — matching καὶ χρόνῳ ἱκανῷ οὐκ ἐνεδύσατο ἱμάτιον; the RP reading attaches ἐκ χρόνων ἱκανῶν to the preceding 'had demons' and puts καί before the garment, which ASV does not.
ASV 'And when he saw Jesus, he cried out' is the same English whether the second participle is joined by καί or not.
ASV 'For he was commanding the unclean spirit' is a progressive past answering the imperfect παρήγγελλεν; the aorist παρήγγειλεν would give 'he commanded'.
ἐδεσμεύετο and ἐδεσμεῖτο are alternative imperfect passives of the same sense; ASV 'and bound with chains and fetters' distinguishes neither.
ASV 'driven of the demon' uses agentive 'of' for ὑπό and ἀπό alike.
ASV 'the demon' renders δαιμονίου and δαίμονος identically.
ASV 'And Jesus asked him, What is thy name?' has no 'saying'; the added λέγων would surface in ASV as 'saying' before the question.
Word order only; 'What is thy name?' is the same English for τί σοι ὄνομά ἐστιν and τί ἐστιν σοι ὄνομα.
Word order only; 'for many demons were entered into him' does not fix the position of εἰσῆλθεν.
ASV 'And they entreated him' has a plural subject, answering παρεκάλουν; the singular παρεκάλει would give 'he entreated'.
ASV 'a herd of many swine feeding on the mountain' leaves the participle's agreement open: 'feeding' can attach to the herd (βοσκομένη) or to the swine (βοσκομένων).
ASV 'and they entreated him that he would give them leave' fits both the aorist παρεκάλεσαν and the imperfect παρεκάλουν.
ASV 'what had come to pass' renders the perfect participle γεγονὸς and γεγενημένον alike.
ASV 'from whom the demons were gone out' is a resultative English perfect that serves the aorist ἐξῆλθεν in a relative clause as readily as the pluperfect ἐξεληλύθει.
ASV reads 'And they that saw it told them how...' with no 'also'; the added adverbial καί (RP 'αὐτοῖς καὶ οἱ ἰδόντες') would appear in ASV as 'also'.
ASV 'all the people of the country ... asked him' leaves the verb's number unmarked, so neither ἠρώτησεν nor ἠρώτησαν is excluded.
ASV text reads 'the country of the Gerasenes' (Γερασηνῶν); the v. 26 note extends 'Gergesenes ... others Gadarenes' to this verse as the reading of other authorities, not of the ASV text.
ASV 'he entered into a boat' is indefinite, answering anarthrous εἰς πλοῖον; the article τὸ would give 'into the boat'.
ASV 'but he sent him away, saying' keeps the subject pronominal; the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς would give 'but Jesus sent him away'.
Word order only; 'how great things God hath done for thee' does not fix σοι before or after ἐποίησεν.
ASV begins 'And as Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him' with no 'it came to pass'; the RP reading Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν would give ASV's usual 'And it came to pass, as ...'.
ASV 'as Jesus returned' renders the articular infinitive alike whether present ὑποστρέφειν or aorist ὑποστρέψαι.
ASV 'and he was a ruler of the synagogue' uses a bare pronoun that answers to οὗτος and αὐτὸς alike.
ASV 'at Jesus’ feet' has no element answering to the article before the name; its presence or absence is invisible in English.
ASV prints 'who had spent all her living upon physicians' in the text and relegates its absence to the mapped note 'Some ancient authorities omit had spent all her living upon physicians, and.'
ASV 'could not be healed of any' uses 'of' for ἀπ᾽ and ὑπ᾽ alike.

ASV prints 'and they that were with him' in the text, with the mapped note showing its absence is only 'some ancient authorities' — so the base reading is excluded; but Treg's καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ and RP's καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ yield the identical English and remain open.
ASV ends Peter's words at 'the multitudes press thee and crush thee'; the added καὶ λέγεις Τίς ὁ ἁψάμενός μου would give 'and sayest thou, Who touched me?', which ASV does not have.
ASV 'that power had gone forth from me' renders the perfect participle ἐξεληλυθυῖαν and the aorist ἐξελθοῦσαν alike in indirect discourse.
ASV reads 'declared in the presence of all the people' with no indirect object; the added αὐτῷ would give 'declared unto him in the presence of all the people'.
ASV's address is simply 'Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole'; Θάρσει would give 'Be of good cheer' before it.
ASV reads 'saying, Thy daughter is dead' with no indirect object; the added αὐτῷ would give 'saying to him'.
ASV 'trouble not the Teacher' carries no 'no more', but the imperative is negated in both readings and ASV may render μηκέτι with a simple prohibition; the English does not settle μηκέτι against μή.
ASV reads 'answered him, Fear not' with no 'saying'; the added λέγων would surface as 'saying' before the words.
ASV 'only believe' does not mark aspect, so the aorist πίστευσον and the present πίστευε are both open.
ASV 'he suffered not any man to enter in with him' renders both τινα and σὺν αὐτῷ; the RP reading οὐδένα has no counterpart for 'with him'.
ASV gives the clause a causal connective, 'Weep not; for she is not dead', answering οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν; RP's asyndetic οὐκ ἀπέθανεν has nothing for 'for'.
ASV reads 'But he, taking her by the hand, called'; the added ἐκβαλὼν ἔξω πάντας καὶ would give 'having put them all forth' before it, which ASV does not have.
ἔγειρε and ἔγειρου are alternative imperative forms of the same verb; ASV 'Maiden, arise' distinguishes neither.
